data.observed_fact: FiaKernelNonQuant owns a shared FiaBlockVecNonQuant<FIAT> vectorService alongside the GQA matmul service and FD service.
Kernel-level ComputeVec1 forwards directly to vectorService.ComputeVec1(info), so the GQA Vec1 slot is serviced by the shared generic vector owner.
Kernel-level ComputeVec2 forwards directly to vectorService.ComputeVec2(info), so the GQA Vec2 slot is serviced by the shared generic vector owner.
Shared Vec1 tiles the M split, calls DealBmm1ResBaseBlock for each tile, optionally injects learnable sink rows, then either exports FD LSE scratch or writes layout-aware softmaxLse output.
Shared Vec1 waits syncC1V1 before ProcessVec1SingleBuf and signals syncV1C2 after it finishes, forming the producer contract for downstream MM2 or FD consumers.

Sink softmax correction subtracts softmaxMaxUb, exponentiates, optionally zeroes invalid split-KV rows through AdjustSoftMaxRes when tndIsS2SplitCore, then accumulates the contribution into softmaxSumUb.

Shared Vec2 tiles M by headDimAlign, rereads mm2ResGm, merges prior split-KV partials from vec2ResGm with softmaxExp, divides by softmaxSum on the last S2 loop, and otherwise writes the next partial back to vec2ResGm.
Shared Vec2 waits syncC2V2 before ProcessVec2SingleBuf and signals syncV2C2 after it finishes, so the C2 to V2 handoff is part of the stage contract.
Generic normal workspace size is the sum of mm1Res, vec1Res, mm2Res, and vec2Res regions, each scaled by preload slots, core count, and their element widths.
Generic nonquant InitWorkspace binds contiguous regions in the fixed order mm1Res, vec1Res, mm2Res, vec2Res, then optional FD accumOut, lseSum, and lseMax.
MLA normal workspace extends the generic four-region sum with an extra nUpdate term and an extra softmaxSum term, one preload-slot-sized slice per core.

MLA InitWorkspace advances offsets only through mm1Res, vec1Res, mm2Res, vec2Res, then optional FD accumOut/lseSum/lseMax; there is no additional named GlobalTensor bound between vec2Res and FD scratch.
Generic FD workspace size is accumOutSize plus logSumExpSize, where accumOut scales with headDimAlign and logSumExp reserves equal-sized sum and max storage.
MLA FD workspace size also splits into accumOut and logSumExp halves, but the parameter count is multiplied by n2Size because each FD reduction task spans MLA heads.
FD LSE scratch is addressed as split-KV-major contiguous regions using combineLseOffset and combineLoopOffset, with lseSumFdGm and lseMaxFdGm read in matching strides per partial.
The first MLA MM2 fixpipe waits syncV1NupdateC2 at the end of the first complete K-slice for the first nL1 and mL1 tile.
On the last S2 loop, MLA Vec1 multiplies softmaxSumUb by the nUpdate scaling term and stores the result in aMlaSumUb for later Vec2 normalization.
MLA Vec2 broadcasts aMlaSumUb and divides bmm2Res by that value before final copy-out, making the stored softmaxSum correction order-sensitive.
GQA MM2 caches V tiles in L1 while canFullLoadV holds and releases V_EVENT only when full-load reuse is impossible or the current mL1 slice is the tail.
FD merge computes weights by colmax over lseMax, exponentiating shifted values, multiplying by lseSum, summing across partials, and normalizing with MatDivsVec.
GQA MM1 caches Q tiles in qL1Snapshot keyed by batch/head/gS1 coordinate and only refills Q_L1 when the signature or required buffer count changes.
s2BaseSize is loaded from metadata S_INNER_SIZE_INDEX and drives the per-task S2 tile width used by task creation and stage kernels.
Host split input forwards mBaseSize and gS1BaseSizeOfFd into splitParam, so M-tile width participates in split-core planning and FD metadata generation.
preLoadNum is a compile-time constant copied into constInfo and governs workspace ring depth plus RunInfo overlap behavior.
nBufferMBaseSize is a compile-time MLA constant that drives n-buffer chunking in MLA MM1, Vec1, MM2, and Vec2 loops.
headDimAlign is derived by Align(headDim, BYTE_BLOCK) and becomes the aligned workspace stride for MM2, Vec2, and FD accumOut paths.
The host split path enables splitKVFlag before workspace sizing, so FD workspace and downstream partial-merge behavior are gated by split routing rather than an inner-kernel constexpr.
Nonquant/GQA ExecuteTask overlaps MM1 on the current slot, Vec1 and MM2 on the older slot, and Vec2 on the previous slot before invalidating that slot.
MLA ExecuteTask uses the same three-slot overlap pattern as the nonquant scheduler: current MM1, older Vec1/MM2, and previous Vec2.
ProcessAmlaNupdate broadcasts row-wise int32 corrections in 128-lane groups and atomically adds them into mm2ResInt32Gm at the current preload-slot offset.
MLA InitWorkspace binds mm2ResInt32Gm as an int32 reinterpretation of mm2ResGm rather than a separate dedicated GM tail region.
aMlaSum is allocated from the local TBuf aMlaSumBuff per preload slot and no workspace SetGlobalBuffer binds it as a dedicated GM region.
MLA Vec1 waits syncC2V1 after ProcessVec1SingleBuf, applies nUpdate, then signals syncV1NupdateC2 for downstream MM2.
Shared Vec1 rounds mSplitSize down to a 32B-safe multiple when SOFTMAX_WITH_BRC is disabled, making UB alignment part of the stage contract.
Shared Vec2 rounds mSplitSize down to a 32B-safe multiple and uses headDimAlign as workspace stride, so alignment and padding stripping are correctness-visible.
FlashDecode reconstructs fdParams from metadata arrays such as bN2IdxOfFdHead, gS1IdxOfFdHead, s2SplitNumOfFdHead, gS1SplitNumOfFdHead, gS1IdxEndOfFdHead, and gS1IdxEndOfFdHeadSplit.
Host SetSplitOutput copies SplitResult.fdRes arrays into tilingData fdParams, forming the bridge between an external split-core producer and kernel FlashDecode consumers.

GQA MM1 splits N and M into 128-sized tiles, applies sparse skip checks before K/Q loads and per-mL1 compute, caches Q_L1 by a batch-head-gS1 signature, and signals syncC1V1 after the fixpipe stage completes.
MLA ComputeMm1 partitions the current M range by nBufferMBaseSize, delegates each chunk to ProcessMm1, and emits syncC1V1 after every n-buffer chunk instead of only once per outer loop.

MLA ComputeMm2 uses the same n-buffer M partitioning, waits syncV1C2 before each ProcessMm2 chunk, then signals both syncC2V2 and syncC2V1 so Vec2 and the Vec1 nUpdate path can observe MM2 completion.

MLA ProcessMm1 uses two fixed K_L1 passes to pack 512-dim key/nope data and 64-dim rope data into L1, reuses QP buffers across mL1 tiles, and fixpipes the ND mm1ResGm ring once the second K_L1 pass finishes.

MLA ProcessMm2 reloads Vec1 output from vec1ResGm, streams V tiles in 256x128 L1 blocks, waits syncV1NupdateC2 before the first fixpipe, and on non-first S-inner loops fixpipes through the mm2ResInt32Gm alias under SetAtomicAdd/SetAtomicNone.
Generic nonquant ComputeMm2 waits syncV1C2, tiles the workload with fixed M/K/N wrapper loops of 256/512/128, delegates the body to DealMm2SingleMKN, and signals syncC2V2 after all tiles complete.

AmlaVecCompute derives nUpdate from the current and previous online max state, converts through exp/cast/cof/eps steps, materializes aMlaSum on the last S2 loop, scales the MM1 result rows in place, and writes an int32 nUpdate vector into outputBuff2.

FlashDecode derives preTokensPerBatch and nextTokensPerBatch from sparseMode, attenMaskFlag, sinkNumber, and actual query/KV lengths, with distinct BAND, DEFAULT_MASK, RIGHT_DOWN_CAUSAL, and LEFT_UP_CAUSAL branches.

FlashDecode final output copy-out switches across BSH, BNSD, NBSD, TND, and NTD layout families by constructing a layout-specific GM tensor wrapper and offset calculator before copying the normalized attention rows.

Host CreateSplitInput packages mBaseSize, s2BaseSize, gS1BaseSizeOfFd, sparse-mode flags, sink counts, and actual-length metadata into SplitParam and BaseInfo before the external split-core planner produces SplitResult.
FlashDecode setup captures the current AIV block index into the service member blockIdx so later merge code can gate work against usedVecNumOfFd and consume the matching fdParams slice.

Host infer-shape normalizes query layouts BSH, BSND, BNSD, NSD, TND, and NTD into canonical batch, sequence, head, and dim axes; attentionOut can be emitted as BSH, BSND, BNSD, NBSD, TND, NTD, or NSD; softmaxLse is shaped as T,N,1 for TND-family inputs and B,N,S1,1 otherwise.

Host mask-parameter packing writes attenMaskFlag, sparseMode, preToken, sinkNumber, keySinkNumber, nextToken, and isRowInvalid into tilingData.maskParams, and forces nextToken to sinkNumber when sink rows are present under SPARSE_MODE_2.

Host invalid-row detection converts BAND and DEFAULT_MASK into left-up window bounds from safe pre/next tokens and reports invalid rows when either derived bound becomes negative, while LEFT_UP_CAUSAL is treated as no-invalid-row and ALL_MASK is always invalid.

MLA Vec1 exports softmaxLse with layout-specific offset formulas: TND uses prefixBS1 and bN2Offset from actualSeqLengthsGmQ, BSH and BSND share the BSND copier, and the remaining branch uses the BNSD copier with qActSeqLensParser.
The MLA kernel reconstructs the same fdParams arrays from metadataGm as the generic kernel, gates entry on usedVecNumOfFd, then SyncAlls before invoking the FD service.

FlashDecode rebuilds per-task scalar offsets by prefix-summing s2SplitNumOfFdHead into combineTaskPrefixSum, multiplying by mBaseSize to form taskOffset, and then adding gS1-part and row offsets for LSE and accumOut access.

MLA Vec2 keeps the same nBufferMBaseSize-driven M partitioning as Vec1, waits syncC2V2 for each partition, and only dispatches ProcessVec2Inner when the current S2 loop is the last one and vecDealM is non-zero.

MLA Vec2 rereads mm2ResGm from the preload-slot ring, zeroes numerically invalid large values, divides rows by aMlaSumUb, then either exports FD partial accumOut or performs layout-aware final copy-out.

TensorPreProcess exits unless both tensor lists exist and both first entries still report DT_INT32, then rewrites each non-null key/value tensor in place by scaling the last view-shape dimension by INT4_NUMS_IN_INT32 and setting the dtype to DT_INT4.

PrefixTensorPreProcess exits unless both prefix tensors exist and still report DT_INT32, then rewrites the last view-shape dimension of each tensor by a factor of 8 and retags both tensors as DT_INT4.

AiInfraFusedInferAttentionSinkProcessSoftmaxLse binds placeHolder to a zero-shape ACL_FLOAT tensor created by aclCreateTensor when softmaxLseFlag is false, and otherwise forwards the caller-provided softmaxLse pointer unchanged.

ProcessTensorContiguous returns nullptr for null input, preserves non-contiguous storage/view metadata by delegating to CalcNoContiguous and CreateView, and otherwise routes the tensor through l0op::Contiguous.

ProcessTensorListContiguous iterates the source tensor list in order, stages nullptr entries, still calls ProcessTensorContiguous on the same iteration, and only reaches AllocTensorList if every loop iteration passes the subsequent CHECK_RET.

ContiguousInput always materializes query through l0op::Contiguous, conditionally materializes each present optional direct tensor, and returns ACLNN_ERR_INNER_NULLPTR if any requested contiguous conversion fails.
The public ACLNN execution entrypoint emits L2_DFX_PHASE_2 and forwards workspace, workspaceSize, executor, and stream unchanged to CommonOpExecutorRun.
MLA CreateSplitInput packages shapes, actual lengths, sparse flags, sink counts, and current split sizes into BaseInfo and SplitParam while forcing supportFD to true for the MLA split planner path.

MLA SetSplitOutput copies SplitResult outer ranges and fdRes arrays into tilingData outerSplitParams and fdParams, including the usedCoreNum * 2 GS1 end-array bridge used by kernel FD metadata reconstruction.
Infer-shape UTs cover TND, BNSD, BSND_BNSD, BSH, and NTD output-shape contracts, including the {0} softmax_lse shape when softmax_lse_flag is false.
Tiling UTs reject negative, over-boundary, and odd sinkNumber values, and validate the supported TND sparse sink path with an expected tiling key and workspace.
Tiling UTs exercise FD, GQA max-workspace, MLA max-workspace, and MLA FD cases with expected workspace vectors and tiling keys.
The op_api UT builds a TND sink case with KV tensor lists, metadata, block table, softmax_lse enabled, and expects TestGetWorkspaceSize to return ACLNN_SUCCESS.
The NPU eager ST builds metadata for a TND sparse sink case, runs npu_fused_infer_attention_sink, and compares output to a Python softmax/matmul reference with 0.004 tolerances.

Graph-capture STs build metadata on an auxiliary stream, wait from the AICore stream, replay the NPU graph, and compare generic and MLA outputs against torch_npu reference attention while also exercising sink-tensor MLA/GQA routing.
Benchmark uses the TND sparse sink scenario, reuses a cached CPU reference output when present, and asserts np.allclose with 0.004 tolerances before optional repeated NPU execution.

data.observed_fact: ComputeMm1 cycles K tiles through kpOrSinkL1BufId, waits on KP_EVENT0 before reusing a L1 buffer, copies K to L1, consumes it through MM1, then releases and wraps the buffer index for the next tile.
KP_EVENT0 uses a paired WaitFlag/SetFlag event cycle across MTE1_MTE2 and MTE2_MTE1 so MTE2 K-copy production and MTE1/MMAD consumption stay ordered.
DealBmm1ResBaseBlock reads MM1 scores from mm1ResGm into UB, runs ElewiseCompute and SoftmaxFlashV2Compute, casts the P tile to KV_T, and writes the result to vec1ResGm for MM2.

The sink-skip branch bypasses the full ElewiseCompute plus SoftmaxFlashV2 path, forwards previous softmax max/sum state, duplicates softmaxExpUb to one, zero-fills vec1ResUb, and writes the zero tile to vec1ResGm.
Both full-M and per-mL1 sparse skip paths call SetFlag on KP_EVENT0 before continuing, preserving event-counter progress even when MMAD work is skipped.
ComputeMm1 performs two IsSkipCal checks, one for the full mSize against nL1 and one for each mL1 block, before deciding whether to skip sparse attention work.
DealMm1SingleMKN enables SetAtomicAdd<MM_OUT_T>() when kStart is nonzero and restores SetAtomicNone after Fixpipe, so later K-split chunks accumulate into mm1ResGm.
ComputeMm1 iterates kStart in K_SPLIT_SIZE chunks and calls DealMm1SingleMKN, whose Fixpipe writes C0 output to mm1ResGm with dstStride set to actualSingleProcessSInnerSizeAlign.
SoftmaxFlashV2Compute updates online softmax max, sum, and exp tensors for each base block and stores the new state in the preload-slot ring.
The first S-inner loop uses softmaxMaxDefaultUb and softmaxSumDefaultUb, while later loops load the previous preload slot's max and sum state.
SoftmaxFlashV2Compute calls SoftMaxFlashV2TilingFunc with per-block source shape, compute type sizes, and softmax temporary-buffer capacity before invoking SoftmaxFlashV2.
The softmax call dispatches between FIA_SOFTMAX_FLASHV2_CFG and FIA_SOFTMAX_FLASHV2_CFG_WITHOUT_BRC according to the compile-time SOFTMAX_WITH_BRC branch.
The sink-skip path copies previous-loop softmaxMaxUb and softmaxSumUb into the current slot, duplicates softmaxExpUb to one, and zeroes the P tile output.
Vec1SinkSoftmaxProc adjusts sink softmax values with AdjustSoftMaxRes using negativeIntScalar and a zero replacement for invalid split-KV rows before accumulating into softmaxSumUb.
DealInvalidMaskRows checks invalid-row and sparse-mask state, then calls fa_base_vector::InvalidMaskRows with softmaxMaxUb, negativeIntScalar, and bmm2ResUb to zero invalid rows in the output path.
SetMSplitInfo maps nBufferDealM to vecDealM as nBufferDealM when <=16, otherwise ceil(ceil(nBufferDealM/16)/2)*16, and odd blockIdx receives the tail remainder.
MLA Vec1 assigns nBufferDealM from nBufferMBaseSize or the tail, computes vecDealM with the same 16-aligned split rule, forces vecDealM to nBufferDealM for CV1:1, and gives odd blockIdx the tail.
FlashDecode computes final LSE with fa_base_vector::ComputeSoftMaxLse using merged lseSumUb and lseMaxUb before layout-aware export.
When invalid rows exist, FlashDecode calls AdjustSoftMaxRes with negativeIntScalar and a 3e+99 replacement before exporting LSE values.
FlashDecode exports LSE through layout-specific DataCopySoftmaxLseTND, DataCopySoftmaxLseNTD, DataCopySoftmaxLseBSND, and DataCopySoftmaxLseBNSD branches.
The TND LSE export path computes a prefixBS1 batch offset and calls DataCopySoftmaxLseTND with vecDealM rows.
The BSND and BSH LSE export path computes a flat batch/head/sequence offset and calls DataCopySoftmaxLseBSND with vecDealM rows.
The BNSD LSE export path dispatches to DataCopySoftmaxLseBNSD with bN2Offset, mOffset, vecDealM, and sequence-length parser state.
Common matmul defines UNITFLAG_DISABLE, UNITFLAG_ENABLE, and UNITFLAG_EN_OUTER_LAST modes and carries unitFlag through MMParam for MMAD lowering.
Matmul assigns mmaParams.unitFlag from param.unitFlag and switches final-K behavior to UNITFLAG_EN_OUTER_LAST for the outer-loop-last K iteration.
Common vector code defines REPEATE_STRIDE_UP_BOUND as 256 and uses columnCount-based repeat strides for vector operations below the wide-column fallback threshold.
Wide-column row sum and row max reduction helpers insert PIPE_V barriers after partial updates and between reduction-halving steps.
Matrix2x2BufferPolicy implements a four-buffer 2x2 policy with M and K cursors, row-first allocation, column-first usage, dynamic m extent, and AllocNext/ReuseNext/FreeNext operations.
PeekNextK returns the next K-dimension buffer cursor for lookahead without advancing the allocation cursor.
The ND-to-NZ copy path divides dValue and srcDValue by HALF_SIZE_DIVISOR for int4b_t before building Nd2NzParams.
Common memory copy defines ND_MATRIX_STRIDE_LIMIT as 65536 and decomposes large source-stride ND-to-NZ copies into CopySingleMatrixNDToNZ calls when the stride exceeds that limit.
FIA_LAYOUT_AXIS_MAP defines canonical axis ordering for more than twenty layouts, including NZ packing as Bn, N, D1, Bs, D0.
FiaTilingShape::GetD returns direct D when present, otherwise derives D from H/N when N divides H, otherwise returns D1*D0 for NZ-style packed layouts.

data.description: Same-name stage functions must preserve canonical_name, owner, owner_qualified, and template identity.
Host and kernel must preserve the contiguous normal workspace order mm1 -> vec1 -> mm2 -> vec2 and append FD regions only with synchronized ABI updates.
GQA MM2 must wait syncV1C2, preserve the V reuse/release guard, and set syncC2V2 around PV compute.
MLA MM2 must wait syncV1NupdateC2 before the first fixpipe that consumes corrected data.
ProcessAmlaNupdate must skip the first S-inner loop and only apply correction on later loops with non-empty M partitions.
ExecuteTask must preserve current-slot MM1, older-slot Vec1/MM2, and previous-slot Vec2 ordering, and may invalidate a slot only after Vec2 completes.
Vec1 and Vec2 must keep 32B-safe mSplitSize rounding and headDimAlign-based workspace stride so UB accesses and copy-out padding remain valid.
When sparse or mask rules produce invalid rows, AdjustSoftMaxRes must run before final softmaxLse export on the last S2 loop.
Vec2 must read the previous preload-slot partial and write the current slot; current and previous vec2ResGm slots must remain distinct.
FlashDecode requires fdParams metadata arrays that map per-core split-KV ranges plus usedVecNumOfFd bounds.
Host SetSplitOutput and kernel FlashDecode readers must agree on usedVecNumOfFd and fdRes array lengths and ordering.
MLA host sizing reserves extra nUpdate and softmaxSum bytes, but current kernel bindings expose nUpdate through normal.mm2 int32 aliasing and no dedicated aMlaSum GM tail.
MLA nUpdate budget bytes must be modeled as a host-budget-only stub whose observed runtime consumer is the normal.mm2 mm2ResInt32Gm alias, not a standalone GM tail.
MLA softmaxSum budget bytes must be modeled as a host-budget-only stub whose observed producer and consumer communicate through aMlaSumUb local UB state.
Host infer-shape, MLA softmaxLse export, and FlashDecode final copy-out must preserve the same canonical layout-family mapping for query axes, attentionOut shapes, and softmaxLse ranks.
Host maskParams packing and kernel sparse branches must preserve sparseMode, preToken, nextToken, sink adjustments, and isRowInvalid semantics.
split_core input params, host SetSplitOutput, and kernel FlashDecode consumers must preserve mBaseSize, s2BaseSize, gS1BaseSizeOfFd, usedVecNumOfFd, and fdRes array ordering.
split_core producer output, host bridge copies, and kernel FlashDecode consumers must preserve fdRes array ordering and per-core BN2/GS1/S2 range semantics.
FD taskOffset prefix sums, preload-slot reload bases, atomic MM2 bases, and headDimAlign padded strides must stay consistent across MLA Vec2, MLA nUpdate, and FlashDecode.
Stage-2 split-core lowering must preserve the common discrete cost model, FA/FD tolerance ratios, sparse/sink/key-sink S2 range shaping, supportFD-gated assignment phases, and FD metadata generation.
Shape validation must use the common ordered layout axis map, derived H=N*D and D derivation rules, NZ {Bn,N,D/D0,Bs,D0} packing with D0=16, and per-axis compare modes including IGNORE_INPUT.

GM copy lowering must derive GmFormat from layout and page-attention state, group offsets by FormatCategory, and preserve ND-to-NZ row count, D extent, source stride, destination NZ C0 stride, int4 divisor, and large-stride fallback behavior.

Vector lowering must preserve repeat-stride thresholds, MAX_VALID_LENGTH split reductions with PIPE_V barriers, safe active-token clamping from actual sequence lengths, and sparse-mode-specific invalid-row handling.

Buffer/event scheduling must preserve BufferType-to-position mappings, hard event pairs, inner-core producer/consumer waits and sets, cross-core event ID legality, policy-owned Init/Uninit, and monotonic BufferManager allocation.
Matmul lowering must preserve UNITFLAG_DISABLE=0, UNITFLAG_ENABLE=2, and UNITFLAG_EN_OUTER_LAST=3, including the final-K-loop-only outer-last behavior in K-split and KPP paths.
Collapsing ComputeMm2 or alias-aware Vec stages across owners hides distinct GQA, MLA, and generic nonquant semantics.
Incorrect V_EVENT release can overwrite reusable V L1 tiles or deadlock the reuse path.
Reordering RunInfo slot responsibilities or invalidating a slot too early can make Vec stages observe stale ring data or deadlock the overlapped pipeline.
Removing Vec1 and Vec2 32B-safe rounding or mishandling headDimAlign can misalign UB accesses and leak padded garbage into outputs.
Skipping invalid-row correction changes the semantic meaning of softmaxLse output and masked rows.
Collapsing current and previous vec2ResGm slots or merging partial and final-output paths can overwrite split-KV partials before FD merge.
Changing AmlaVecCompute order can alter nUpdate correction numerics.
Missing SetAtomicNone or wrong broadcast stride can corrupt MLA MM2 accumulation.
Wrong LSE max/sum offsets or merge weights corrupt split-KV final output.
Producer/consumer disagreement on fdParams arrays or usedVecNumOfFd bounds can send FlashDecode to the wrong partial ranges.
Treating MLA host-budget-only tail bytes as dedicated GM tensors invents nonexistent producer/consumer paths and corrupts Stage-2 validation and lowering.
Lowering MLA nUpdate as a standalone GM tail instead of the observed normal.mm2 int32 alias can move atomic correction away from the MM2 data it adjusts.
Inventing a GM producer or consumer for MLA softmaxSum hides the observed aMlaSumUb local-buffer bridge and can mis-specify Vec2 normalization ordering.
Reordering or resizing workspace regions without synchronized host and kernel ABI updates can redirect ring slots or FD scratch to the wrong bytes.
Changing infer-shape or layout-specific exporters independently can mismatch attentionOut and softmaxLse tensor ranks or offsets across BSH, BSND, BNSD, NBSD, TND, and NTD families.
Divergence between host maskParams packing and kernel sparse or invalid-row branches can invert sink-window or row-validity semantics.
Divergence in split_core range packing silently reassigns BN2, GS1, or S2 work across FD tasks and makes host fdParams disagree with kernel FlashDecode consumers.

Omitting common split-core cost, tolerance, core-search, sparse/sink/key-sink, or assignment semantics can produce a Stage-2 planner that preserves array names while assigning different BN2/GS1/S2 ranges and FD work.
Omitting common axis maps, derived dimensions, NZ packing, or compare modes can make Stage-2 accept layouts that host validation rejects or reject valid TND/NZ/dense families.
Omitting common GmFormat, FormatCategory, OffsetCalculator, and ND-to-NZ lowering semantics can address the wrong GM rows or copy invalid packed tiles into L1/UB.
Omitting common buffer hard-event pairs, cross-core event ID rules, or policy lifetimes can introduce deadlocks, double-use live buffers, or illegal AIC/AIV producer-consumer ordering.
Omitting common safe-token clamping and invalid-row helpers can lose sparse-mode-specific zeroing or PIPE_V barriers, changing masked rows and softmax outputs.
Omitting common FD RecordFDInfo and SplitFD balancing semantics can make generated fdParams structurally valid but inconsistent with split-KV vector merge boundaries.
